reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents an easy passive-income opportunity tied to a Uniswap front-running bot and uses prominent large-profit claims to attract participation. It directs viewers to deploy and fund a contract with Ether to place transactions around another user's pending transaction. The returns are described as variable, and the records do not independently establish that the software works, that the returns occurred as described, or that the transactions were safe.

citations.quote: In this YouTube video tutorial I'll be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income.
So now we will deploy this to our wallet.
the next step is to fund our contract with some Ethers to be able to snipe liquidity
the victim's transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we make a profit. From the slippage difference in the transaction.
Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week to week.

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise a fixed or guaranteed return. It expressly warns viewers that performance can vary and that the strategy is sometimes unprofitable. That qualification matters: the profit examples are presented as personal results, not as a certainty for every user. A careful viewer is given a material limitation before deciding whether the approach is worthwhile. The content therefore reads as conditional financial commentary about a volatile trading technique, not an assurance that depositing Ether will inevitably produce income.

citations.quote: Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week to week.
I've had some weeks where I made 5-6 Ethers.
But usually I make 2 plus Ethereum a week.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes dramatic examples but omits the explicit warning that profitability is inconsistent. Calling the activity front-running describes the proposed trading method; it does not establish that the speaker guaranteed returns or concealed risk. The supplied material also does not independently prove that the examples were fabricated or that the software failed.

citations.quote: Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week to week.
This is going to allow us to sniff the pending transactions that are not yet mined
the balance from the bot is now in my wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the overall solicitation. The same speaker calls the method an easy way to make passive income and reports gains of roughly 17% and nearly 40%, while instructing viewers to fund the contract. Saying results sometimes fluctuate still leaves the dominant impression that substantial profits are normally available; it does not establish that the bot works for viewers or that the shown balance came from trading profits.

citations.quote: I'll be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income.
I have something around 1.17 Ether, which is around 17%.
Something close to 40%, which isn't that bad

opening.argument: The material is structured as a hands-on programming and blockchain demonstration. It explains what Remix is, selects a Solidity compiler version, creates a contract file, deploys it, checks the contract on Etherscan, and describes its controls. Those are concrete operational steps a learner could inspect and reproduce. The subject is therefore an educational explanation of smart-contract tooling and transaction ordering, even if the presenter also discusses a personal use case. A tutorial format is not, by itself, proof that every claim is a solicitation or a deceptive offer.

citations.quote: Remix, which is a web application that allows us to develop, deploy, compile, and launch smart contracts coded in the Solidity language.
Now head over to the left sidebar and create a new file named bot.sol.
Under Compiler select the version 0.6.6 so it will match our contract.
As we can see here, there are four actions for a contract.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats instructional steps as proof of a scam outcome. But the record shows a recognizable development workflow: code is pasted, compiled, deployed, and checked. Explaining how pending transactions and gas priority work can be technical education even when the subject is controversial. The prosecution identifies no supplied evidence that the code secretly diverted funds or that the deployment screen was fabricated.

citations.quote: Remix, which is a web application that allows us to develop, deploy, compile, and launch smart contracts coded in the Solidity language.
Head back to Etherscan and paste it. Yep, it was created successfully.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely how the appeal is delivered, but it does not make the financial claims educationally neutral. The tutorial tells viewers to deploy to their wallet, fund the contract, and start it, then attributes later balances to the bot. Code compilation and an on-chain contract address show only that a contract was deployed, not that it performs profitable front-running or is safe to fund.

citations.quote: So now we will deploy this to our wallet.
the next step is to fund our contract with some Ethers
So the bot will continue to run until you press the Withdraw button.
The last step is to click Start.

opening.argument: At most, this is promotion of software and a blockchain service workflow, not evidence of a classic scam structure. The supplied material does show a funding step, but it does not show a request for passwords, seed phrases, identity documents, recruiting a downline, or payment for access to a guaranteed-return program. It also describes a withdrawal control and says the results are not always profitable. Those omissions matter: the record does not establish credential theft, referral income, or a guaranteed deposit-return mechanism. The product can be evaluated as an automated trading tool whose performance remains uncertain.

citations.quote: Download software version - https://telegra.ph/Uniswap-Front-Running-Bot-2022-11-19
Withdrawal will stop the bot and transfer funds back to your wallet.
Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week to week.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls the funding instruction inherently deceptive, but funding is also the ordinary operational requirement for a trading contract. The record does not show that the creator requested account credentials or promised a fixed return. It describes a withdrawal function and acknowledges losses or fluctuating performance, which are inconsistent with a plainly guaranteed-return pitch.

citations.quote: Withdrawal will stop the bot and transfer funds back to your wallet.
Sometimes it's not always profitable, and profits fluctuate week to week.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely an ordinary purchase: viewers are told to place Ether into a contract and are encouraged to add more because larger deposits supposedly enable larger trades and profits. The absence of a seed-phrase request or referral scheme does not answer whether the offered bot works. A withdrawal button and variable-results disclaimer do not prove that deposited funds will be returned or that the claimed profits came from the bot.
